patterns.pattern: Biallelic NOTCH3 mutations split into two distinct, non-overlapping phenotypic and chronological syndromes based strictly on variant molecular consequence
patterns.abstraction: A single genetic locus can manifest as two non-continuous clinical diseases where complete loss-of-function yields severe pediatric developmental arrest, while structural missense variants yield delayed adult-onset neurodegeneration.
patterns.instance: In the global cohort of 50 biallelic NOTCH3 patients, 26 with loss-of-function null variants presented in infancy (9 to 14 months) with developmental delay, seizures, spasticity, and early strokes, whereas 24 with cysteine-involving missense variants presented in early adulthood (3rd to 5th decades) with classic CADASIL-like subcortical ischemic events and dementia.
patterns.direction: Establish formal separate clinical and OMIM sub-classifications for pediatric biallelic NOTCH3 loss-of-function leukoencephalopathy versus adult biallelic cysteine-altering CADASIL.
patterns.support: Strong pooled evidence from 50 clinically and genetically characterized patients evaluated across multiple international multicenter cohorts.

patterns.hypothesis: NOTCH3 loss-of-function disrupts early cerebrovascular developmental signaling causing mural hypoplasia, whereas cysteine-involving missense variants cause toxic, age-dependent extracellular GOM accumulation.
patterns.novelty: Refutes the concept of recessive NOTCH3 disease as a phenotypic continuum or simple homozygous CADASIL, revealing two mutually exclusive pathogenic entities under OMIM #621295.

patterns.pattern: Variant-specific spatial neuroimaging topography: periatrial leukomalacia-like volume loss distinguishes biallelic loss-of-function from temporal-predominant CADASIL patterns
patterns.abstraction: Mutational classes within the same gene drive mutually exclusive anatomical lesion topographies on neuroimaging.
patterns.instance: Biallelic loss-of-function NOTCH3 variants cause periatrial and periventricular white matter volume loss mimicking periventricular leukomalacia accompanied by microcalcifications, whereas cysteine-altering missense variants consistently cause deep white matter hyperintensities and early anterior temporal pole lesions.
patterns.direction: Develop automated MRI volumetric and topographic scoring systems that quantify periatrial volume loss versus anterior temporal hyperintensity to rapidly sort pediatric vascular leukodystrophies.
patterns.support: Consistent neuroimaging correlations observed in multiple independent cohorts totaling 26 loss-of-function and 24 missense cases.

patterns.hypothesis: Periatrial white matter watershed areas are uniquely vulnerable to developmental flow impairment caused by biallelic loss of vascular smooth muscle NOTCH3 signaling.
patterns.novelty: Identifies periventricular leukomalacia phenocopying in full-term infants without hypoxic-ischemic birth injury as a specific diagnostic clue for recessive NOTCH3 loss-of-function arteriopathy.

patterns.pattern: Diagnostic discrimination via negative phenotypes: systematic absence of anterior temporal lesions and extraneurological CARASIL signs rules out primary phenocopies
patterns.abstraction: Obligate negative discriminators (features consistently absent in the target condition) offer higher diagnostic specificity than shared core neuroimaging or stroke manifestations.
patterns.instance: Sparing of the anterior temporal pole on T2/FLAIR reliably discriminates pediatric biallelic loss-of-function NOTCH3 patients from classic CADASIL, while the complete absence of premature alopecia (HP:0002297) and degenerative spondylosis (HP:0003419) rules out CARASIL (HTRA1).
patterns.direction: Construct negative-feature diagnostic decision algorithms for early-onset genetic small vessel diseases.
patterns.support: Multi-cohort validation where anterior temporal pole sparing occurred in 3/3 assessed patients and extraneurological CARASIL features were absent across biallelic NOTCH3 cohorts.

patterns.hypothesis: Tissue-restricted pathology in NOTCH3 loss-of-function reflects cerebral-specific dependence on NOTCH3 signaling, unlike HTRA1 which regulates TGF-beta in hair follicles and intervertebral discs.
patterns.novelty: Establishes that negative neuroradiological signs (anterior temporal sparing) and absent systemic findings together differentiate recessive NOTCH3 disease from both dominant CADASIL and recessive CARASIL.

patterns.pattern: Low penetrance of peripheral cutaneous microvascular signs limits their utility as gating diagnostic criteria
patterns.abstraction: Peripheral microvascular manifestations in systemic monogenic arteriopathies often demonstrate incomplete penetrance, rendering them unsuited as mandatory clinical diagnostic criteria.
patterns.instance: Cutaneous vascular signs such as livedo reticularis or livedo racemosa occur in under 35% of pediatric biallelic NOTCH3 loss-of-function patients, being documented as absent in 2/2 siblings in one cohort and seen only intermittently in others.
patterns.direction: Standardize systemic dermatologic examination combined with skin punch biopsies across all suspected pediatric genetic arteriopathies to determine true subclinical vascular penetrance.
patterns.support: Cross-cohort observations indicating absence or low frequency of livedo manifestations across pediatric series.

patterns.hypothesis: Cerebral small vessels possess lower collateralization and higher wall-shear stress than cutaneous microvessels, allowing loss of NOTCH3 function to cause severe encephalopathy while cutaneous vessels remain subclinically compensated.
patterns.novelty: Challenges the clinical reflex to require cutaneous signs like livedo reticularis before suspecting primary vascular leukodystrophies in pediatric stroke patients.

patterns.pattern: Apparent spatial lesion overlap emerges as an artifact of end-stage cerebral atrophy rather than primary disease predilection
patterns.abstraction: Advanced diffuse neurodegeneration can obscure early pathognomonic spatial signatures, creating apparent contradictions in lesion distribution between early and late disease stages.
patterns.instance: Apparent temporal lobe white matter hyperintensities in adolescent homozygous loss-of-function patients (such as a 12-year-old Moroccan proband) reflect generalized white matter rarefaction and end-stage atrophy rather than the early, selective anterior temporal pole hyperintensity characteristic of CADASIL.
patterns.direction: Implement longitudinal, stage-stratified neuroimaging protocols to differentiate early selective white matter hyperintensity topography from late-stage generalized parenchymal volume loss.
patterns.support: Reconciliation of conflicting reports showing strict temporal sparing in early childhood cohorts (3/3 patients) contrasted with temporal signal alterations in advanced adolescent probands.

patterns.hypothesis: The anterior temporal pole white matter in biallelic loss-of-function patients is structurally preserved during early disease stages and undergoes signal change only secondary to pan-cortical deafferentation and end-stage parenchymal loss.
patterns.novelty: Resolves a published literature contradiction by showing that late-stage temporal atrophy phenocopies primary CADASIL-like temporal pole lesions.
